rule content: TypeNodes(P, m) = { t | t ∈ Type ∧ Subnode(ASTModule(P, m), t) }

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 3. Project and Compilation Model > 3.2 Project Root and Manifest paragraph @608
When project loading begins from one command-line input path `p`, the implementation MUST first resolve any relative `p`
rule content: When project loading begins from one command-line input path `p`, the implementation MUST first resolve any relative `p` against the host current working directory before searching upward for `Cursive.toml`. If that resolved path denotes an existing non-directory, the upward search MUST begin from its parent directory; otherwise the upward search MUST begin from the resolved path itself. `FindProjectRoot(p)` is the nearest searched directory `R` such that `exists(R/`Cursive.toml`)`; if no searched directory satisfies that predicate, `FindProjectRoot(p)` is the search-start directory.

 p[2..|p|)  if UNC(p)

JoinComp(c::cs) =

 b  if AbsPath(b)

rule content: Float literals MAY omit a suffix when they contain a decimal point. The suffix `f` indicates a float literal with width inferred from context; explicit suffixes `f16`, `f32`, `f64` specify the width directly. BeforeSuffixUnderscore(s) ⇔ ∃ suf ∈ NumSuffix. EndsWith(s, Concat("_", suf))
NumericUnderscoreOk(s) ⇔ ¬ StartsWithUnderscore(s) ∧ ¬ EndsWithUnderscore(s) ∧ ¬ AfterBasePrefixUnderscore(s) ∧ ¬ AdjacentExponentUnderscore(s) ∧ ¬ BeforeSuffixUnderscore(s)

rule content: DecRun(T, i) = max({i} ∪ { j | i < j ≤ |T| ∧ ∀ k ∈ [i, j). (DecDigit(T[k]) ∨ T[k] = "_") })
HexRun(T, i) = max({i} ∪ { j | i < j ≤ |T| ∧ ∀ k ∈ [i, j). (HexDigit(T[k]) ∨ T[k] = "_") })
OctRun(T, i) = max({i} ∪ { j | i < j ≤ |T| ∧ ∀ k ∈ [i, j). (OctDigit(T[k]) ∨ T[k] = "_") })
BinRun(T, i) = max({i} ∪ { j | i < j ≤ |T| ∧ ∀ k ∈ [i, j). (BinDigit(T[k]) ∨ T[k] = "_") })
SuffixMatch(T, i, U) = max({i} ∪ { j | i < j ≤ |T| ∧ Lexeme(T, i, j) ∈ U })

DecCoreEnd(T, i) =
 ExpEnd(T, q)  if p = DecRun(T, i) ∧ p < |T| ∧ T[p] = "." ∧ q = DecRun(T, p+1)
 ExpEnd(T, p)  if p = DecRun(T, i) ∧ (p ≥ |T| ∨ T[p] ≠ ".")

NumericCoreEnd(T, i) =
 HexRun(T, i+2)  if T[i..i+2] = "0x"
 OctRun(T, i+2)  if T[i..i+2] = "0o"
 BinRun(T, i+2)  if T[i..i+2] = "0b"
 DecCoreEnd(T, i)  otherwise
NumericScanEnd(T, i) = SuffixMatch(T, NumericCoreEnd(T, i), NumSuffix)
HasDot(T, i, j) ⇔ ∃ p. i ≤ p < j ∧ T[p] = "."
HasExp(T, i, j) ⇔ ∃ p. i ≤ p < j ∧ T[p] ∈ {"e", "E"}
HasFloatCore(T, i, j) ⇔ HasDot(T, i, j)

NumericKind(T, i) =
 FloatLiteral  if HasFloatCore(T, i, NumericCoreEnd(T, i)) ∨ SuffixMatch(T, NumericCoreEnd(T, i), FloatSuffixSet) > NumericCoreEnd(T, i)
 IntLiteral    otherwise

**(Lex-Int)**
DecDigit(T[i])    j = NumericScanEnd(T, i)    NumericKind(T, i) = IntLiteral
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ IntLiteral(T, i) ⇓ j

**(Lex-Float)**
DecDigit(T[i])    j = NumericScanEnd(T, i)    NumericKind(T, i) = FloatLiteral
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ FloatLiteral(T, i) ⇓ j
NumericLexemeOk(T, i, j) ⇔ (Lexeme(T, i, j) matches integer_literal ∨ Lexeme(T, i, j) matches float_literal) ∧ NumericUnderscoreOk(Lexeme(T, i, j))
NumericLexemeBad(T, i, j) ⇔ ¬ NumericLexemeOk(T, i, j)

**(Lex-Numeric-Err)**
DecDigit(T[i])    j = NumericScanEnd(T, i)    NumericLexemeBad(T, i, j)    c = Code(Lex-Numeric-Err)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ Emit(c, SpanOfText(S, i, j))

rule content:
**(Lex-String)**
Lexeme(T, i, j) matches string_literal
────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ StringLiteral(T, i) ⇓ j
BackslashCount(T, p) = max{ k | 0 ≤ k ≤ p ∧ ∀ r ∈ [p-k, p). T[r] = "\\" }
UnescapedQuote(T, p) ⇔ T[p] = "\"" ∧ BackslashCount(T, p) mod 2 = 0
StringTerminator(T, i) = min{ q | q > i ∧ (UnescapedQuote(T, q) ∨ T[q] = LF ∨ q = |T|) }
LineFeedOrEOFBeforeClose(T, i) ⇔ StringTerminator(T, i) = |T| ∨ T[StringTerminator(T, i)] = LF
EscapeMatch(T, p, q) ⇔ Lexeme(T, p, q) matches escape_sequence ∧ EscapeOk(Lexeme(T, p, q))
BadEscapeAt(T, p) ⇔ T[p] = "\\" ∧ ¬ ∃ q. EscapeMatch(T, p, q)
FirstBadEscape(T, i) = min{ p | i < p < StringTerminator(T, i) ∧ BadEscapeAt(T, p) }

**(Lex-String-Unterminated)**

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ Emit(c, SpanOfText(S, i, i+1))

**(Lex-String-BadEscape)**
FirstBadEscape(T, i) = p    c = Code(Lex-String-BadEscape)
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ Emit(c, SpanOfText(S, p, p+1))

**(Lex-Char)**
Lexeme(T, i, j) matches char_literal
─────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ CharLiteral(T, i) ⇓ j

CharScalarCountFrom(T, p, q) = 1 + CharScalarCountFrom(T, r, q) ⇔ p < q ∧ T[p] = "\\" ∧ EscapeMatch(T, p, r)
CharScalarCountFrom(T, p, q) = 1 + CharScalarCountFrom(T, p+1, q) ⇔ p < q ∧ T[p] = "\\" ∧ ¬ ∃ r. EscapeMatch(T, p, r)
CharScalarCount(T, i) = CharScalarCountFrom(T, i+1, CharTerminator(T, i))

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 8. Type System Core > 8.4 Metatheoretic Properties paragraph @6236
rule content: This subsection states the key metatheoretic properties that the Cursive type system is designed to satisfy. Formal proofs are deferred to supplementary materials.

**(Progress)**
If Γ ⊢ e : T and `e` is not a value, then either:
1. `e` can take a step.
2. `e` is blocked on an external operation.
3. `e` panics.

**(Preservation)**
If Γ ⊢ e : T and `e → e'`, then Γ ⊢ e' : T.

**(No-Use-After-Free)**
A binding in state `Moved` or `PartiallyMoved(F)` where `f ∈ F` cannot be read or moved from.

**(No-Double-Free)**
Each responsible binding is dropped exactly once when it goes out of scope.

**(No-Dangling-Pointers)**
A pointer `Ptr<T>@Valid` always references valid storage. A pointer with provenance `π` cannot escape to storage with longer lifetime `π'` where `π < π'`.

**(Exclusivity-Invariant)**
If a binding `x` has permission `unique` and is in state `Active`, then no other live path exists to the same storage location.

**(Permission-Preservation)**
Permissions are preserved as permission regimes. Admissibility at a use site MUST NOT create a weaker alias or convert a `unique` binding into `shared` or `const`.

**(State-Determinism)**
At each program point, every binding has exactly one state in `{Valid, Moved, PartiallyMoved(F)}`.

**(No-Resurrection)**
A binding in state `Moved` cannot transition back to `Valid` except through reassignment of a `var` binding.

**(Data-Race-Freedom)**
Concurrent accesses to `shared` data are serialized through the key system.

**(Fork-Join-Guarantee)**
All work items spawned within a `parallel` block complete before the block exits.

**(Key-Serialization)**
If two tasks hold keys `K₁` and `K₂` to overlapping paths with incompatible modes, the key system ensures they do not execute concurrently.

**(Async-Key-Safety)**
Keys cannot be held across `yield` or `wait` suspension points unless the `release` modifier is used.

rule content: 9. A `[[log]]` attribute list MAY appear as a standalone statement with no trailing expression. The observed value is `()` and the observed type is `()`. If `expected` is present, it MUST type-check against `()`.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 9. Attributes and Metadata > 9.5 Diagnostics and Metadata Attributes > 9.5.4 Static Semantics requirement 10
rule content: 10. When `expected` is an identifier, it MUST resolve to a binding visible in the current scope. The binding's type MUST be equality-comparable with the observed value type. The binding MUST be in `Alive` state with `const` or `unique` permission.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 9. Attributes and Metadata > 9.5 Diagnostics and Metadata Attributes > 9.5.5 Dynamic Semantics requirement 4

rule content: 5. For a `Procedure` target, one entry record MUST be emitted at procedure entry, and one exit record MUST be emitted on each normal return. When the return type is non-unit, the exit record MUST include the return value as `actual`.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 9. Attributes and Metadata > 9.5 Diagnostics and Metadata Attributes > 9.5.5 Dynamic Semantics requirement 6
rule content: 6. Each emitted record MUST include a thread identifier and a global monotonically increasing emission sequence number. Within one execution thread or task, emitted records MUST preserve source execution order. Across threads and tasks, the externally observable log order MUST be ascending emission sequence number.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 9. Attributes and Metadata > 9.5 Diagnostics and Metadata Attributes > 9.5.5 Dynamic Semantics requirement 7
rule content: 7. Log-emission failure MUST NOT change program semantics.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 9. Attributes and Metadata > 9.5 Diagnostics and Metadata Attributes > 9.5.5 Dynamic Semantics requirement 8
rule content: 8. For a `Statement` target, one log record MUST be emitted containing the source site, optional `label`, and `actual = ()`.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 10. Permissions and Binding State > 10.3 Binding Activity States > 10.3.4 Static Semantics paragraph @7033
rule content: A binding `b` with `unique` permission exists in one of two states:
State=Active | Definition=No suspended admissible uses of `b` are live | Operations Permitted=Read, write, move
State=Inactive | Definition=A non-consuming admissible use of `b` is currently live | Operations Permitted=No direct operations on `b`

**(Inactive-Enter)**
b : `unique` T    b is Active    non-consuming admissible use of b begins
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
b becomes Inactive

**(Inactive-Exit)**
b is Inactive    all live non-consuming admissible uses of b end
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
b becomes Active with `unique` permission preserved

rule name: During the inactive period, the original `unique` binding MUST NOT be read, written, or moved.
rule content: During the inactive period, the original `unique` binding MUST NOT be read, written, or moved.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 10. Permissions and Binding State > 10.3 Binding Activity States > 10.3.5 Dynamic Semantics paragraph @7054

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 14. Abstraction and Polymorphism > 14.8 Refinement Types > 14.8.4 Static Semantics paragraph @13252

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 14. Abstraction and Polymorphism > 14.8 Refinement Types > 14.8.7 Diagnostics paragraph @13269
rule content: Diagnostics are defined for ill-formed or impure refinement predicates, failed static proof obligations for refinement introduction, and failing dynamic refinement checks.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 15. Procedures and Contracts > 15.3 Overloading > 15.3.4 Static Semantics paragraph @14232
rule content: Free-procedure overload resolution is complete before ordinary `Call` typing.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 15. Procedures and Contracts > 15.3 Overloading > 15.3.4 Static Semantics paragraph @14234
rule content: For a free call whose callee names an overload set `O`:

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 15. Procedures and Contracts > 15.3 Overloading > 15.3.4 Static Semantics requirement 1
rule content: 1. Candidate selection: retain procedures in `O` whose parameter count equals the argument count.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 15. Procedures and Contracts > 15.3 Overloading > 15.3.4 Static Semantics requirement 2
rule content: 2. Type filtering: eliminate candidates for which any argument is incompatible with the corresponding parameter under the call-argument compatibility rules of §16.3.4.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 15. Procedures and Contracts > 15.3 Overloading > 15.3.4 Static Semantics requirement 3
rule content: 3. Exact-match preference: if multiple candidates remain, retain those with the maximal number of exact argument-type matches.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 15. Procedures and Contracts > 15.3 Overloading > 15.3.4 Static Semantics requirement 4
rule content: 4. Genericity preference: if both generic and non-generic candidates remain, retain only the non-generic candidates.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 15. Procedures and Contracts > 15.3 Overloading > 15.3.4 Static Semantics requirement 5
rule content: 5. Constraint specificity: if multiple generic candidates remain, retain only those whose bounds and predicate requirements are pointwise at least as specific as every remaining alternative, with at least one strict improvement.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 15. Procedures and Contracts > 15.3 Overloading > 15.3.4 Static Semantics requirement 6
rule content: 6. If exactly one candidate remains, that candidate is selected.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 15. Procedures and Contracts > 15.3 Overloading > 15.3.4 Static Semantics requirement 7
rule content: 7. If no candidate remains, the call is ill-formed with `E-SEM-3031`.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 15. Procedures and Contracts > 15.3 Overloading > 15.3.4 Static Semantics requirement 8
rule content: 8. If multiple candidates remain after all preference stages, the call is ill-formed with `E-SEM-3030`.

rule name: Two visible overloads with the same name MUST NOT have identical parameter-mode/type signatures after generic-parameter
rule content: Two visible overloads with the same name MUST NOT have identical parameter-mode/type signatures after generic-parameter erasure. Such a declaration set is ill-formed with `E-SEM-3032`.
When `LookupMethod(T, name) = m`, execution uses that unique method body. No runtime overload search is performed.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 15. Procedures and Contracts > 15.3 Overloading > 15.3.6 Lowering paragraph @14253
rule content: Overload resolution is complete before lowering. Lowering consumes the selected procedure or method symbol only.
Code=`E-SEM-3030` | Severity=Error | Detection=Compile-time | Condition=Ambiguous overload resolution
Code=`E-SEM-3031` | Severity=Error | Detection=Compile-time | Condition=No matching overload found
Code=`E-SEM-3032` | Severity=Error | Detection=Compile-time | Condition=Duplicate signature in overload set

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 22. Compile-Time Execution and Metaprogramming > 22.4 Quote, Splice, and Emission > 22.4.2 Parsing paragraph @24317
rule content: CaptureQuotedTokens(P) ⇓ (P', ts) consumes the balanced token sequence between the opening `{` at `P` and its matching `}` and preserves nested delimiter structure and all splice markers inside that slice.

**(Parse-Quote-Raw)**
IsIdent(Tok(P))    Lexeme(Tok(P)) = "quote"    IsPunc(Tok(Advance(P)), "{")    CaptureQuotedTokens(Advance(P)) ⇓ (P_1, ts)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ ParsePrimary(P) ⇓ (P_1, QuoteNode(⊥, QuotedRaw(ts), SpanBetween(P, P_1)))

**(Parse-Quote-Type)**
IsIdent(Tok(P))    Lexeme(Tok(P)) = "quote"    IsKw(Tok(Advance(P)), `type`)    IsPunc(Tok(Advance(Advance(P))), "{")    CaptureQuotedTokens(Advance(Advance(P))) ⇓ (P_1, ts)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ ParsePrimary(P) ⇓ (P_1, QuoteNode(`Type`, QuotedRaw(ts), SpanBetween(P, P_1)))

**(Parse-Quote-Pattern)**
IsIdent(Tok(P))    Lexeme(Tok(P)) = "quote"    FixedIdentTok(Tok(Advance(P)), `pattern`)    IsPunc(Tok(Advance(Advance(P))), "{")    CaptureQuotedTokens(Advance(Advance(P))) ⇓ (P_1, ts)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ ParsePrimary(P) ⇓ (P_1, QuoteNode(`Pattern`, QuotedRaw(ts), SpanBetween(P, P_1)))

rule content: `quote { ... }`, `quote type { ... }`, and `quote pattern { ... }` are valid only in compile-time contexts.
ResolveQuoteKind(QuoteNode(kind, body, span), T_exp) = kind    if kind ≠ ⊥

ResolveQuoteKind(QuoteNode(⊥, body, span), T_exp) = kind    if ExpectedAstKind(T_exp) = ⊥ ∧ `kind` is the unique member of {`Expr`, `Stmt`, `Item`} for which `ParseQuotedBody(kind, body)` succeeds

rule content: If an `Ast` splice occupies identifier or binding position, `HygienizeAst` MUST preserve the original binding structure of the spliced fragment.

rule content: `emitter~>emit(ast)` is well-formed only when `emitter` has compile-time type `TypeEmitter` and `ast` has compile-time type `Ast::Item` or `Ast`.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 22. Compile-Time Execution and Metaprogramming > 22.4 Quote, Splice, and Emission > 22.4.5 Dynamic Semantics paragraph @24390
rule content:
ParseQuotedBody(`Expr`, QuotedRaw(ts)) ⇓ payload iff the ordinary expression parser, extended with `SpliceExprNode` and `SpliceIdentNode`, parses `ts` as exactly one expression.
ParseQuotedBody(`Stmt`, QuotedRaw(ts)) ⇓ payload iff the ordinary statement parser, extended with `SpliceExprNode` and `SpliceIdentNode`, parses `ts` as exactly one or more statements.
ParseQuotedBody(`Item`, QuotedRaw(ts)) ⇓ payload iff the ordinary item parser, extended with `SpliceExprNode` and `SpliceIdentNode`, parses `ts` as exactly one or more top-level items.
ParseQuotedBody(`Type`, QuotedRaw(ts)) ⇓ payload iff the ordinary type parser, extended with `SpliceExprNode` and `SpliceIdentNode`, parses `ts` as exactly one type.
ParseQuotedBody(`Pattern`, QuotedRaw(ts)) ⇓ payload iff the ordinary pattern parser, extended with `SpliceExprNode` and `SpliceIdentNode`, parses `ts` as exactly one pattern.
RenderSplice(`Expr`, cv) ⇓ payload    iff (cv = CtAst(a) ∧ AstKindOf(a) = `Expr` ∧ payload = AstPayloadOf(a)) ∨ (cv ≠ CtAst(_) ∧ Γ ⊢ CtLiteralize(cv) ⇓ payload)
RenderSplice(`Stmt`, cv) ⇓ payload    iff cv = CtAst(a) ∧ AstKindOf(a) ∈ {`Stmt`, `Expr`} ∧ payload = AstPayloadOf(a)
RenderSplice(`Item`, cv) ⇓ payload    iff cv = CtAst(a) ∧ AstKindOf(a) = `Item` ∧ payload = AstPayloadOf(a)
RenderSplice(`Type`, cv) ⇓ payload    iff (cv = CtAst(a) ∧ AstKindOf(a) = `Type` ∧ payload = AstPayloadOf(a)) ∨ (cv = CtType(T) ∧ payload = T)
RenderSplice(`Pattern`, cv) ⇓ payload iff cv = CtAst(a) ∧ AstKindOf(a) = `Pattern` ∧ payload = AstPayloadOf(a)
RenderSplice(`Identifier`, cv) ⇓ payload iff cv = CtString(name) ∧ payload = Identifier(name)

rule name: HygienizeAst(a, quote_site, emit_site, n) ⇓ (a', n') MUST satisfy all of the following:

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 22. Compile-Time Execution and Metaprogramming > 22.4 Quote, Splice, and Emission > 22.4.5 Dynamic Semantics requirement 1
rule content: 1. Any capture from the quote site resolves to the same binding after emission.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 22. Compile-Time Execution and Metaprogramming > 22.4 Quote, Splice, and Emission > 22.4.5 Dynamic Semantics requirement 2
rule content: 2. Any binder introduced by hygienic quoted content MUST NOT capture names from the emission site unless the splice was string-valued in identifier position.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 22. Compile-Time Execution and Metaprogramming > 22.4 Quote, Splice, and Emission > 22.4.5 Dynamic Semantics requirement 3
rule content: 3. Fresh hygienic marks are deterministic functions of `quote_site`, `emit_site`, and the input counter `n`.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 22. Compile-Time Execution and Metaprogramming > 22.4 Quote, Splice, and Emission > 22.4.5 Dynamic Semantics paragraph @24413
rule content: `QuoteBuild` evaluates splice expressions in left-to-right source order. Each splice value is rendered by `RenderSplice`, substituted into the quoted payload, and the resulting fragment becomes the payload of the returned `Ast`.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 22. Compile-Time Execution and Metaprogramming > 22.4 Quote, Splice, and Emission > 22.4.5 Dynamic Semantics requirement 1
rule content: 1. derive-generated emissions required by §22.5 for the current declaration

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 22. Compile-Time Execution and Metaprogramming > 22.4 Quote, Splice, and Emission > 22.4.5 Dynamic Semantics requirement 2
Cursive Language Specification > 22. Compile-Time Execution and Metaprogramming > 22.4 Quote, Splice, and Emission > 22.4.6 Lowering paragraph @24426
rule content: Quoted and spliced AST fragments affect lowering only through the declarations and expressions present after Phase 2 expansion. No runtime representation of `Ast` survives unless explicitly embedded by emitted declarations.

rule name: Cursive Language Specification > 22. Compile-Time Execution and Metaprogramming > 22.5 Derive Targets and Contracts > 22.5.2 Parsing paragraph @24448
rule content: `[[derive(... )]]` is parsed by the attribute parser in §9.1.2; the `derive` attribute name and its argument list are interpreted by this section.

**(Parse-DeriveTargetDecl)**
IsIdent(Tok(P))    Lexeme(Tok(P)) = "derive"    FixedIdentTok(Tok(Advance(P)), `target`)    Γ ⊢ ParseIdent(Advance(Advance(P))) ⇓ (P_1, name)    IsPunc(Tok(P_1), "(")    FixedIdentTok(Tok(Advance(P_1)), `target`)    IsPunc(Tok(Advance(Advance(P_1))), ":")    IsIdent(Tok(Advance(Advance(Advance(P_1)))))    Lexeme(Tok(Advance(Advance(Advance(P_1))))) = "Type"    IsPunc(Tok(Advance(Advance(Advance(Advance(P_1))))), ")")    Γ ⊢ ParseDeriveContractOpt(Advance(Advance(Advance(Advance(Advance(P_1)))))) ⇓ (P_2, contract_opt)    Γ ⊢ ParseBlock(P_2) ⇓ (P_3, body)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ ParseItem(P) ⇓ (P_3, DeriveTargetDecl(name, contract_opt, body, SpanBetween(P, P_3), []))

**(Parse-DeriveContractOpt-Yes)**
IsOp(Tok(P), "|:")    Γ ⊢ ParseDeriveClauseList(Advance(P)) ⇓ (P_1, clauses)
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ ParseDeriveContractOpt(P) ⇓ (P_1, clauses)

**(Parse-DeriveClauseList-Cons)**
Γ ⊢ ParseDeriveClause(P) ⇓ (P_1, clause)    Γ ⊢ ParseDeriveClauseTail(P_1, [clause]) ⇓ (P_2, clauses)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ ParseDeriveClauseList(P) ⇓ (P_2, clauses)

**(Parse-DeriveClause-Requires)**
FixedIdentTok(Tok(P), `requires`)    Γ ⊢ ParseIdent(Advance(P)) ⇓ (P_1, name)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ ParseDeriveClause(P) ⇓ (P_1, ⟨`requires`, name⟩)

**(Parse-DeriveClause-Emits)**
FixedIdentTok(Tok(P), `emits`)    Γ ⊢ ParseIdent(Advance(P)) ⇓ (P_1, name)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Γ ⊢ ParseDeriveClause(P) ⇓ (P_1, ⟨`emits`, name⟩)

rule name: Execution of the body follows ordinary procedure semantics. Boundary panic handling is defined by §23.7. When `UnwindMode(proc)
rule content: Execution of the body follows ordinary procedure semantics. Boundary panic handling is defined by §23.7. When `UnwindMode(proc) = "catch"`, the boundary MUST return `ZeroValue(R)` for the raw exported procedure's return type `R`.

rule name: For a raw exported procedure `proc` owned by a project `P` satisfying `RawExportLibrary(P)`, a boundary call occurs only
rule content: For a raw exported procedure `proc` owned by a project `P` satisfying `RawExportLibrary(P)`, a boundary call occurs only through one live loaded library image `i` owned by `P`. Before the first raw export call through a newly loaded image, the implementation MUST establish that image by `LibraryImageInitSigma(P, i, σ)` as defined in §24.4.4. Later raw export calls through the same live image MUST reuse the same image-owned static state, poison flags, and boundary panic record until unload. On unload of that live image, the implementation MUST execute `LibraryImageDestroySigma(P, i, σ)` exactly once. User-procedure execution within that live image is governed by `RawLibraryCallSigma(P, i, proc, vs, σ)` in §24.4.4.

rule name: For any shared library project `P`, an ordinary Cursive call that crosses a shared-library link boundary into one extern
rule content: For any shared library project `P`, an ordinary Cursive call that crosses a shared-library link boundary into one externally linked procedure owned by `P` likewise occurs only through one live loaded library image `i` owned by `P`. Before the first such linked call through a newly loaded image, the implementation MUST establish that image by `LibraryImageInitSigma(P, i, σ)` as defined in §24.4.4. Later linked calls through the same live image MUST reuse the same image-owned static state, poison flags, and boundary panic record until unload. On unload of that live image, the implementation MUST execute `LibraryImageDestroySigma(P, i, σ)` exactly once. User-procedure execution for that linked call continues to follow ordinary `ApplyProcSigma` under the image-state interpretation defined by §24.4.4.

rule content:
These lifecycle exports MUST NOT propagate `Panic` across the foreign boundary. rule name: A raw export call from foreign code on `RawExportLibrary(P)` occurs only with one live loaded library image `i` owned by
rule content:
A raw export call from foreign code on `RawExportLibrary(P)` occurs only with one live loaded library image `i` owned by `P`. Before the first raw export call through a newly loaded image, the implementation MUST establish that live image by `LibraryImageInitSigma(P, i, σ)`. Later raw export calls through the same live image MUST reuse that image-owned state. On library unload of that live image, the implementation MUST execute `LibraryImageDestroySigma(P, i, σ)` exactly once.
An ordinary Cursive call that crosses a shared-library link boundary into `SharedLibrary(P)` likewise occurs only with one live loaded library image `i` owned by `P`. Before the first such linked call through a newly loaded image, the implementation MUST establish that live image by `LibraryImageInitSigma(P, i, σ)`. Later linked calls through the same live image MUST reuse that image-owned state. On library unload of that live image, the implementation MUST execute `LibraryImageDestroySigma(P, i, σ)` exactly once.
On targets whose shared-library linker selects one loader entrypoint symbol for process attach/detach, a conforming backend MUST emit exactly one backend-generated loader entrypoint for each linked image of `SharedLibrary(P)`. That loader entrypoint is not a user-declared `ProcedureDecl`. It MUST establish `LibraryImageInitSigma(P, i, σ)` before user code first becomes callable from that image, MUST execute `LibraryImageDestroySigma(P, i, σ)` on image unload, and MUST NOT expose any additional capability-bearing parameter to Cursive user code.

rule content:
EscapeBytes(e) =
  EscapeValue(e)          if e = `"\u{"` h_1 … h_n `"}"`
  [EscapeValue(e)]        otherwise

StringBytesFrom(T, p, q) =
  []                                                        if p = q
  EscapeBytes(Lexeme(T, p, r)) ++ StringBytesFrom(T, r, q)  if p < q ∧ T[p] = `"\\"` ∧ EscapeMatch(T, p, r)
  EncodeUTF8(T[p]) ++ StringBytesFrom(T, p + 1, q)          if p < q ∧ T[p] ≠ `"\\"`
StringBytes(lit) = bytes ⇔ lit.kind = StringLiteral ∧ T = Lexeme(lit) ∧ StringBytesFrom(T, 1, |T|-1) = bytes

Cursive Language Specification > Appendix B. Complete Grammar Reference paragraph @29261
rule content: This appendix consolidates canonical grammar productions into one parser-oriented reference.
code_point      ::= (* Unicode scalar except U+000A and prohibited code points *)
string_char      ::= (* Unicode scalar except ", \\, or U+000A *)
char_content ::= (* Unicode scalar except ', \\, or U+000A *)
primitive_type ::= integer_type | float_type | bool_type | char_type | unit_type | never_type | string_type | bytes_type
range_expression    ::= exclusive_range | inclusive_range | from_range | to_range | to_inclusive_range | full_range
postfix_suffix ::= "." identifier | "." decimal_literal | "[" expression "]" | "~>" identifier "(" argument_list? ")" | "(" argument_list? ")" | "?"

primary_expr ::= literal | identifier_expr | path_expr | tuple_literal | array_literal | record_literal | closure_expr | if_expr | loop_expr | block_expr | comptime_expr | quote_expr | quote_type | quote_pattern | type_literal
literal ::= integer_literal | float_literal | string_literal | char_literal | bool_literal | null_literal | unit_literal

if_tail        ::= block_expr ("else" (block_expr | if_expr))?
                 | "is" pattern block_expr ("else" (block_expr | if_expr))?
                 | "is" "{" if_case+ if_case_else? "}"
pattern                ::= literal_pattern | wildcard_pattern | identifier_pattern | tuple_pattern | record_pattern | enum_pattern | modal_pattern | range_pattern

statement ::= binding_decl terminator | assignment_stmt terminator | compound_assign terminator | expr_stmt | return_stmt | break_stmt | continue_stmt | defer_stmt | region_stmt | frame_stmt | unsafe_block | key_block_stmt | comptime_stmt
place_expr      ::= identifier | postfix_expr "." identifier | postfix_expr "[" expression "]"

top_level_item ::= import_decl | using_decl | static_decl | procedure_decl | comptime_procedure_decl | record_decl | enum_decl | modal_decl | class_declaration | type_alias_decl | extern_block | derive_target_decl

using_clause    ::= module_path "::" identifier ("as" identifier)?
                  | module_path "::" using_list
                  | module_path "::" "*"
procedure_decl ::= attribute_list? visibility? "procedure" identifier generic_params? signature predicate_clause? contract_clause? block_expr?
method_def         ::= attribute_list? visibility? "override"? "procedure" identifier generic_params? "(" receiver ("," param_list)? ")" ("->" return_type)? contract_clause? block_expr
record_decl       ::= attribute_list? visibility? "record" identifier generic_params? implements_clause? predicate_clause? "{" record_body "}" invariant_clause?
record_field_decl ::= attribute_list? visibility? identifier ":" type record_field_init?
enum_decl       ::= attribute_list? visibility? "enum" identifier generic_params? implements_clause? predicate_clause? "{" variant_members? "}" invariant_clause?
modal_decl        ::= attribute_list? visibility? "modal" identifier generic_params? implements_clause? predicate_clause? "{" state_block+ "}" invariant_clause?
state_method_def  ::= attribute_list? visibility? "procedure" identifier generic_params? state_method_signature contract_clause? block_expr
transition_def    ::= attribute_list? visibility? "transition" identifier "(" param_list ")" "->" "@" target_state block_expr
class_declaration   ::= attribute_list? visibility? "modal"? "class" identifier generic_params? ("<:" superclass_bounds)? predicate_clause? "{" class_item* "}"
class_item          ::= abstract_procedure | concrete_procedure | abstract_field | abstract_state | associated_type
type_alias_decl ::= attribute_list? visibility? "type" identifier generic_params? predicate_clause? "=" type
foreign_procedure ::= attribute_list? visibility? "procedure" identifier generic_params? signature predicate_clause? contract_clause? foreign_contract_clause_list? terminator
dispatch_expr        ::= "dispatch" pattern "in" range_expression key_clause? dispatch_option_list? block_expr
comptime_procedure_decl ::= attribute_list? "comptime" visibility? "procedure" identifier generic_params? signature requires_clause? block_expr
foreign_procedure            ::= attribute_list? visibility? "procedure" identifier generic_params? signature predicate_clause? contract_clause? foreign_contract_clause_list? terminator
